_note: Black holes for /explore v2 Slice 6. Three real (M87*, Sagittarius A*, Cygnus X-1) with cited parameters, one fictional (Gargantua, Kip Thorne's Interstellar model — badged fiction). Rendered with a geodesic gravitational-lensing shader. Placement: Sag A* reuses its S5 galactocentric spot; M87* + Cygnus X-1 by RA/Dec direction on the sky-sphere (like deep-sky); Gargantua is fictional, flagged. Masses in solar masses, distances in light-years, spin is the dimensionless a* (0..~1), rs_km is the Schwarzschild radius. inclination_deg is the disk tilt used for the render framing. Mass and distance of the real holes are the published values named in each `catalogue` entry (scripts/refresh-black-hole-catalogue.mjs); rs_km is recomputed from the mass.

objects.name: Sagittarius A*
objects.discovery: Event Horizon Telescope image 2022; mass from GRAVITY Collaboration 2022

mass_solar.source: GRAVITY Collaboration 2022, Mass of Sgr A* and distance to the Galactic Centre

dist_ly.source: GRAVITY Collaboration 2022, Mass of Sgr A* and distance to the Galactic Centre
dist_ly.note: 8.277 +/- 0.009 (stat) +/- 0.033 (sys) kpc to the Galactic Centre; SIMBAD lists no distance for this object, so the value is not cross-checked there

objects.name: M87*
objects.discovery: First black hole ever imaged — Event Horizon Telescope 2019

mass_solar.source: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration 2019 (paper VI), M87* shadow, mass and distance
mass_solar.note: 6.5 +/- 0.7 billion solar masses (gas and stellar dynamics put it near 6.6 billion: Kormendy & Ho 2013, 2013ARA&A..51..511K)

dist_ly.source: Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration 2019 (paper VI), M87* shadow, mass and distance
dist_ly.note: adopted distance to M87, 16.8 +/- 0.8 Mpc; SIMBAD compiled distances 53881.0 to 64383.3 kly (n=8), consistent; Cosmicflows-4 gives M87 55.0 million ly

objects.name: Cygnus X-1
objects.discovery: First widely accepted stellar-mass black hole; mass revised upward Miller-Jones et al. 2021

mass_solar.source: Miller-Jones et al. 2021, Cygnus X-1 contains a 21-solar mass black hole

dist_ly.source: Miller-Jones et al. 2021, Cygnus X-1 contains a 21-solar mass black hole
dist_ly.note: 2.22 +0.18/-0.17 kpc from radio parallax; SIMBAD compiled distances 6.8 to 7.7 kly (n=4), consistent

objects.name: Gargantua
objects.discovery: Fictional — Kip Thorne's physically-modelled black hole for Interstellar (2014)
